predictions.selection_reason: external chunk size -> pointer advancement calculation -> critical for safe buffer traversal
predictions.source_summary: ptr points to external FLI/FLC animation data buffer provided as input parameter buf; advance value is read from first 4 bytes of current chunk header
predictions.sink_summary: ptr advancement used to traverse chunk data structure; bytes counter decremented to track remaining buffer size; potential buffer overrun if advance exceeds remaining bytes
predictions.guard_summary: Initial bytes >= 4 check; chunk processing loop has bytes < 10 check; individual chunk handlers have bounds checks; but no validation that advance value is reasonable relative to remaining bytes
predictions.risk_pattern: External chunk size value (advance) used directly for pointer arithmetic without validation against remaining buffer size, potentially leading to out-of-bounds memory access
called_function_context: I32 macro (reads 4 bytes as little-endian integer)
predictions.context_summary: FLI/FLC animation decoder processing chunks in a loop; each chunk has 6-byte header with type and size; advance reads chunk size from header to move to next chunk
unresolved_facts: Whether Python wrapper validates chunk sizes before calling this function
Whether there are additional validation checks in calling code
Exact security implications of the specific change from ptr += I32(ptr) to advance = I32(ptr); ptr += advance;

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: External chunk size value read from buffer header used for pointer advancement without validation against remaining buffer size, leading to potential out-of-bounds memory access

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
top_sast_rules.description: A 'for' loop that increments its loop variable but checks it against a lower bound, or decrements its loop variable but checks it against an upper bound, will either stop iterating immediately or keep iterating indefinitely, and is usually indicative of a typo.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a potentially malicious tarball using `shutil.unpack_archive()` without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can cause files outside the destination directory to be overwritten. More precisely, if the tarball comes from a user controlled location either a remote one or cli argument.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.
